title: P3: acquire_with Err site 3 (Decision::Failed after a failed break rmdir) has no test; the_two_sampling_refusals test names it but only exercises site 2
description: From the T6 security review F3 + follow-up (p2-pre-w4a-review.md §Task 6): of acquire_with's six Err sites, site 3 (Decision::Failed, reached only from resolve_stale_with's rmdir ERROR arms, FsError::Exists / FsError::Other) has no test. Site 3 is currently unreachable from the harness: SpyFs::rmdir delegates unconditionally to RealFs with no failure-injection knob. Not blocking: the arm follows a FAILED rmdir (the peer's directory was not removed, so no completed break exists), record: None is a literal one arm below the Ok(()) => Some(record) arm, and the pass-through carries any future draft anyway. Do: rename the test to name site 2 only + a comment pointing at the two rmdir-error arms; add an rmdir-failure knob (FsError::Exists) and a site-3 test only if S22 needs rmdir-failure injection anyway, and only after agctl-pmh (the ungated cancel_after_rmdir hook) is fixed — the test doubles need a fidelity pass before growing another knob.

title: Linux support: file-only credential backend on platforms without a keychain (post-W5)
description: Scope: platforms without the macOS login keychain (Linux first). Claude Code there uses only the plaintext store <dir>/.credentials.json (0600; dir = CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude); no secret-service/libsecret backend exists in 2.1.26x (the backend factory is a stub, D-020), so agentctl must not add one either. Design: select the keychain layer by target platform at build time (cfg(target_os = "macos") keeps security(1) / KW1; other unix targets get a file-only backend where the live store is <dir>/.credentials.json under the same three-lock protocol and the same WriteTarget/audit discipline). The existing testing seam AGENTCTL_KEYCHAIN_BACKEND=none already models 'no keychain at all' and is the shape to promote into a real platform backend, not a runtime knob. Consequences: I15 (4032-byte line), refusal D, R27, PM10 and the security(1) argv hygiene do not apply on file-only targets; ACL/prompt concerns (V6/R30) do not exist; discovery of foreign items reduces to the live file plus agentctl-owned namespaces. Non-goals: Windows; any Linux secret-service integration; changing macOS behaviour. Evidence to carry: the composed-read facts recorded from the 2.1.263 binary must be re-verified on a Linux build of Claude Code before implementation. Filed on the user's order 2026-09-10 after the lead's answer to 'what replaces /usr/bin/security on Linux'; scheduled after W5 (blocked by S25 and S26).

title: P2: use --live wedges (refusal F, then NewerCopy forever) when D's item already holds an older credential of the account being swapped in — third_namespace does not exclude the incoming record

Fails closed (no credential lost, 0 keychain writes). Root cause: D-017's adoption matrix has no row for 'the displaced credential is a stale copy of the incoming account's own'. Fix: add that row (discard the stale copy — the refreshed pair already lives in the incoming store — and skip the third-namespace adoption), exclude the incoming record from third_namespace, e2e for the shape. Design decision for W4b's contract too.

title: P2: use --live cannot swap in an account whose own store has migrated to the keychain (item-only incoming credential is refused in Phase A)
description: From W4a fix loop 3 disclosure 1 (p2-w4a-s22-report.md §F9.9): the forward swap reads the incoming credential only from its plaintext .credentials.json (Incoming::credentials), so an Owned account whose store Claude Code has migrated (item present, file absent) is refused in Phase A with refusal F / exit 14 — the loop-3 fix corrects the advice text; the capability is missing. Fix: read the incoming credential from its keychain item (location::from_keychain under the incoming namespace's own lock/identity checks, the S21 read path), and when the swap refreshes it, persist the refreshed pair back into that item through the three-lock protocol on the INCOMING namespace (a second hold, sequenced before Phase C on the target) or refuse-with-pointer to status as today (NEEDS_REFRESH). Needs its own contract section; candidate for W4b's contract alongside the live store, or W5. Related: agctl-bk5 (reverse-direction write-back).

Also lets use --undo of a first write know the store was removed without inferring it.

Fix: write the refreshed credential back to ADOPTED_FILE under D's namespace lock before Phase C, via the staging path P1-1 protects (stage → commit before the hold, since this copy IS the credential's home). Until then the undo's note must warn when the restored credential was refreshed.

title: P3: held_locks::read_all lists the held-locks directory with a path-based fs::read_dir, so the reader still follows a symlink the writer now refuses
description: From the pre-W4a lane's T4 report and the T4 security review (p2-pre-w4a-review.md §Task 4, finding 1, re-graded P3 → P2): after agctl-p2-held-locks-dir-through-symlink-1yj the WRITER reaches held-locks through an O_NOFOLLOW walk, but held_locks::read_all still enumerates with fs::read_dir(&dir) by path and only opens each record file O_NOFOLLOW (consumers: doctor's held-locks section and the --remove-stale permit). Fix: open_dir_under(namespace_root(), held-locks) and enumerate through the dirfd (rustix::fs::Dir), opening each record fd-relative; same fix site as the doctor diagnosis gap (see the bead filed with it). Schedule before W4b (the live-store swap widens the blast radius).

title: P3: lock-protocol error wording — held-locks refusal reuses Unreachable ('cannot be locked'), Compromised says 'was modified' for an unreadable mtime, TakeFailure::Io asserts a filesystem fault for a likely contention
description: Merged wording bead (T4 review F4 + T5 review F1/F2). (1) write_held_record maps a refused walk to LockError::Unreachable whose Display says the store directory 'cannot be locked' and whose doc says 'down to the store directory' → add LockError::RecordUnreachable { path, message } ('the held-lock record directory cannot be used'), keep status's LockUnavailable mapping, pin the string in the symlink test. (2) After axs, LockError::Compromised ('was modified while agentctl held it') also fires for (Some, None), where nothing was observed to move → wording that covers 'could not be re-read'. (3) take_all's TakeFailure::Io text asserts a filesystem fault, but after a successful mkdirat a None mtime most likely means ENOENT (someone removed the lock we just took) — a contention signal → say 'disappeared or could not be read'. All three reach the user via status's free-form note; nothing pins the strings; no audit consumer.

title: P3: use --live maps every acquire Err (LockError) to refusal letter A, so 'A' does double duty for lock-compromised and for unreachable/busy-like acquire failures
description: From the W4a fix lane's residual 5 (p2-w4a-s22-report.md §F6): after P2-3 a failed keychain write has its own exit code (WRITE_FAILED=19) and refusal: null, but the acquire's Err path (AcquireFailure.error: LockError::Unreachable / RecordUnreachable / Io / WrongTree) still maps to refusal A ('lock compromised'). It contradicts no audit line, but the letter is not a security signal when it also covers a planted symlink at held-locks or an unreadable mtime. Fix: a distinct exit code + refusal null (or a new letter reserved by the plan) for acquire failures that are not the drift check; keep A for drift_check only. Coordinate with agctl-get (lock-protocol error wording).

title: P3: log_writer release window strands a log line written between is_held() and the buffer take (signal/panic paths)

A pass thread that observed held=true and appends after the take leaves bytes nobody flushes. Harmless on the q path (emergency() and drop(terminal) release twice); on the signal and panic paths one teardown log line can be lost. Fix: check the flag under the buffer lock in write() and clear it under the same guard in release_terminal_to(); no syscall under the lock.

title: P2: a completed lock break's BreakDraft is dropped on every Err return out of acquire_with (six sites), so the peer's lock can be removed with no audit entry (I16)
description: From the T4 security review addendum (p2-pre-w4a-review.md §Task 4 'Addendum: break-then-Unreachable'), amended by the T5 review. In claude_lock::acquire_with the break rule rmdirs the peer's stale lock and returns Decision::Broken { record: Some(draft) }; the draft sits in a local Option<BreakDraft> and reaches the audit log only through Ok(Acquisition { break_record }) at its single caller (status.rs refresh_in_place). Every Err return after the break drops it — six sites: the pre-mkdir refusals that can follow a break, write_held_record's Err (deterministic via a symlink at held-locks after 1yj; also ENOSPC/EACCES/name exhaustion), and the take failures — and after axs the take-failure site is reachable with no mkdir failure at all (an unreadable mtime right after our own mkdirat). BreakDraft has no Drop; only a tracing::info! breadcrumb without the record's fields survives. Fix: Result<Acquisition, AcquireFailure> with AcquireFailure { error: LockError, break_record: Option<BreakDraft> }, every Err site passing the draft it holds (no From<LockError> shortcut), the caller appending before mapping to LockUnavailable; a test per Err site asserting the audit line. Not a per-site probe (TOCTOU, fixes no invariant). GATES the W4a wave close; does not gate 1yj/axs.
close_reason: Landed: acquire/acquire_with return Result<Acquisition, AcquireFailure { error, break_record }> with no From<LockError> (a ? cannot drop a draft); all six Err sites pass the draft; refresh_in_place appends it once, unconditionally, before every mapping. Review APPROVE + verify PASS (p2-pre-w4a-review.md / -verify.md §Task 6), 993 tests. W4a wave gate passed; caller-side e2e tracked as i9o (S22 dependency); site-3 test as 169; knob fidelity as pmh.

title: P1 (W4b gate): Tree::Live cannot lock a symlinked ~/.claude; naive fix would lock $HOME/.claude.lock instead of the peer's realpath(dir).lock
description: w2-rereview P1 (p2-w2-rereview.md). LockAnchor::open anchors Tree::Live at store_dir.parent() and walks the last component with O_NOFOLLOW (claude_lock.rs:589-607, file_store.rs:1035-1055), so live_store_dir()=$HOME/.claude being a symlink (F41, this machine) yields LockError::Unreachable permanently. title: P2: with fd 1 closed at exec, output silently succeeds (exit 0) — signals::install's self-pipe can be allocated fd 1 before dispatch
description: completions-verify gap 1 (reproduced 3/3): 'agentctl completions zsh >&-' exits 0 with empty stderr and nothing written, while the same with stdout as a file delivers 34,357 bytes. Hypothesis (no dtruss in the sandbox): main() calls signals::install (signal_hook self-pipe) before dispatch; with fd 1 closed the lowest free fd is 1, so later writes to stdout land in the self-pipe. Affects every command's stdout, not only completions. Fix: detect a closed fd 0/1/2 at startup (fcntl(F_GETFD)) and reopen them on /dev/null (the conventional daemon-safe move) or refuse with a message; add an e2e that spawns the binary with fd 1 pre-closed. Hand to S25/W5 or a runtime follow-up.

title: P3: KeychainWriteError::Failed { stderr } carries unbounded child output (review P2-6)
description:
p2-w2-review.md P2-6. Real security -i does not echo its input on a parse error (verified), so no
demonstrated leak; still cap stderr to a few hundred bytes and strip anything hex-like before it
reaches an error message.

W3 review delta (2026-09-10, p2-w3-review.md). Two things S21 changed that this bead predates:

1. The path now has a PRODUCTION caller. When this was filed, keychain_write::write_item had none;
   src/commands/status.rs's refresh-in-place is the first, so the exposure is live from that commit.
2. The string now reaches status --json. write_item's failure path puts err.to_string() into
   outcome.note, which is rendered to the terminal AND into the machine-readable JSON note field,
   not just a terminal line. KeychainWriteError::Failed's Display embeds the raw, unbounded stderr
   of the one child in the crate whose stdin held the plaintext credential.

Remediation now has two halves: cap and scrub in run_write as originally filed, AND classify at the
point of display, e.g. note: Some(match &err { Failed { class, .. } => format!("the keychain refused
the write ({class:?})"), other => other.to_string() }), so the JSON field carries the class the user
can act on rather than bytes. Refuse to surface stderr at all if it contains a run of >= 32 lowercase
hex characters. Severity stays P3.
notes: S22 delta (p2-w4a-review.md P3-4): a security(1) child's stderr reaches the user's terminal verbatim from use --live's failed-write arm. Fix once in keychain_write: cap and classify the stderr (the ten-class classifier exists for reads), surface a class name, never the raw bytes.

title: P3: a migrated namespace's item is read three times before the POST and renders as two rows
description:
W3 review (2026-09-10, p2-w3-review.md) ruling (c). src/provider/claude/discovery.rs, the migration probe and the owned/unclaimed rows.

One pass over a migrated namespace reads the same keychain item three times before any refresh: foreign_activity::detect confirming the migration, discovery parsing it for the owned row, and discovery parsing it AGAIN for the 'unclaimed' row it also emits, because a migrated namespace's service is not a CLAIMED one. AC43 evidence: a job spawns /bin/sleep 30, hands the Child to the coordinator via PassCtx::register_child, and reports its pid to the test over a handshake channel; the test then cancels and asserts (a) the results drain and the channel disconnects -- which is precisely 'workers joined', since each worker owns one Sender -- within a measured 500 ms of cancellation, (b) the job's wait_child returned ErrorKind::Interrupted, meaning the coordinator killed the child rather than it exiting on its own, and (c) 'ps -p <pid>' is empty, so the child is dead and reaped. title: P2: HeldLocks::release rmdirs by name after refusal A, so agentctl can remove a lock it no longer holds
description:
W3 review (2026-09-10, p2-w3-review.md). src/secret/claude_lock.rs:966-978 (release), reached from src/commands/status.rs refusal A.

drift_check returning Compromised means a third party touched a lock agentctl holds, which includes the case where the directory was removed and RECREATED by somebody else. compromised() returns, HeldLocks::Drop runs release(), and release() does unlinkat(parent_fd, name, AT_REMOVEDIR) for each artefact BY NAME. It removes whatever directory now bears that name, which may be the new holder's lock: a removal outside the two circumstances invariant I11' permits, and it is not audited.

Bounded (a legitimate peer would have had to see our lock stale, and the primary's window is 60s against a <=3s hold), so the drift has to be malicious or a clock step. But the identity check drift_check just performed is thrown away instead of being carried into the release.

Remediation: have release skip (and warn/record) any artefact whose mtime no longer matches the recorded one, rather than rmdir-ing by name unconditionally.

Now on the default status --refresh path (S21), which is why the review raised its urgency.
